quizzes.title: SCO and IORA: Practice MCQs
quizzes.passage:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is a Eurasian grouping that brings together a number of states from the region. Its core objective is regional cooperation to counter terrorism, separatism and extremism. Its membership grew over time, and India joined in 2017, which strengthened India's engagement with Central Asia, a region where geographical constraints limit direct access. Taken together, the grouping's members account for a large share of the world's economic output and population.

Within the grouping, a regional body coordinates counter-terrorism work and intelligence sharing among members. Its emphasis on security is sometimes seen as overshadowing its economic and development cooperation. Border disputes and political frictions between some members are among the factors that affect constructive engagement.

The Indian Ocean Rim Association is a different kind of body. It is an intergovernmental organisation that promotes cooperation among countries bordering the Indian Ocean. Its areas of cooperation include maritime safety, fisheries management, trade facilitation and disaster risk management. Its vision was shaped during a visit to India by a prominent leader. The association also supports a track-based forum, the Indian Ocean Dialogue, which brings together policymakers, strategic experts and maritime stakeholders. The forum was first launched in Australia, and India has hosted several of its editions.

questions.q: Which country joined the Shanghai Five after its 1996 formation, turning the grouping into the SCO in 2001?
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan's entry in 2001 turned the Shanghai Five into the SCO, while the other three were original members.

questions.q: Where is the SCO's Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) based?
questions.explanation: RATS is based in Tashkent.

questions.q: In which year was the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) established?
questions.explanation: IORA was established in 1997, while 1995 is the year of the visit that inspired its vision.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Council of Heads of States is the SCO's supreme decision-making body.
Reason (R): The SCO's official languages are Russian and Chinese.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the language fact does not explain the body's decision-making role.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure
II. IORA Secretariat
III. SCO Secretariat
IV. Indian Ocean Dialogue launch
A. Ebene
B. Beijing
C. Tashkent
D. Perth
questions.explanation: RATS is in Tashkent, the IORA secretariat in Ebene, the SCO secretariat in Beijing, and the Dialogue was launched in Perth.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The SCO's secretariat is located in Ebene, Mauritius.
II. The IORA's secretariat is located in Ebene, Mauritius.
III. The Indian Ocean Dialogue was first launched in 2013.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The IORA secretariat is in Ebene and the Dialogue began in 2013, while the SCO secretariat is in Beijing.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) The SCO has observers including Mongolia.
(b) The IORA was established in 1995.
(c) The SCO's secretariat is located in Beijing.
questions.explanation: Statements (a) and (c) are correct, while IORA was established in 1997, so statement (b) is wrong.

quizzes.title: SCO and IORA: Type-in Answers
quizzes.passage:
This passage covers two regional bodies with interests in Asia and the Indian Ocean. The first is a Eurasian grouping that began as a group of five states. It later expanded, and its membership now includes India and several Central Asian states. Its supreme decision-making body is a Council of Heads of States. The grouping accounts for about 30% of global GDP and about 40% of the world population. Its stated aim is regional cooperation against terrorism, separatism and extremism. Its structures include a regional anti-terrorist body that shares intelligence among members. For India, membership offers a route into a region that geography makes hard to reach directly.

The second is an intergovernmental organisation for countries that border the Indian Ocean. It was established in 1997 and has its secretariat in Mauritius. Its vision came out of a 1995 visit to India by a prominent leader. Its areas of cooperation include maritime safety and security, fisheries management and disaster risk management. A track-based forum, the Indian Ocean Dialogue, brings together policymakers, strategists and maritime stakeholders, and its objectives include maritime security cooperation and regional connectivity. The forum is a Track 1.5 diplomatic platform under the association. It was first launched in Australia in 2013, and India has since hosted several editions.

questions.q: In which year did the grouping become the SCO after Uzbekistan joined?
questions.explanation: The Shanghai Five became the SCO in 2001 after Uzbekistan joined.

questions.q: In which year was the Shanghai Five formed?
questions.explanation: The Shanghai Five emerged in 1996.

questions.q: In which city is the SCO secretariat located?
questions.explanation: The SCO secretariat is in Beijing.

questions.q: Which town in Mauritius hosts the IORA secretariat?
questions.explanation: The IORA secretariat is in Ebene (Mauritius).

questions.q: Whose 1995 visit to India inspired the vision behind IORA? Give the full name.
questions.explanation: IORA's vision originated during Nelson Mandela's 1995 visit to India.

questions.q: What are the two official languages of the SCO? Give both.
questions.explanation: The SCO's official languages are Russian and Chinese.

questions.q: In which year, apart from 2014 and 2021, did India host an Indian Ocean Dialogue edition?
questions.explanation: India hosted Indian Ocean Dialogue editions in 2014, 2019 and 2021.

quizzes.title: Korea, Komagata Maru and Sikkim: Practice MCQs
quizzes.passage:
The Korean peninsula was divided after the Second World War, and the division has shaped its politics ever since. A dividing line still marks the border between the two states, and a demilitarised zone lies along it. North Korea came under Soviet influence and South Korea under American influence, which deepened the divide. A war then broke out when troops from the north crossed that line, prompting the UN Security Council to condemn the invasion.

The history of Sikkim also shows how political arrangements can change a region's status. Earlier, British-era treaties had already tied the territory to British India. A Himalayan kingdom ruled by a hereditary royal dynasty came under Indian protection through an agreement, with India taking charge of defence, external affairs and communications. Later, the territory's status changed further, and after a popular vote it became a full state of India. Its identity and land rights are protected by a constitutional provision.

Another episode involves a ship that carried passengers from India towards Canada. The passengers were mostly Sikhs, with some Muslims and Hindus, and they hoped for economic opportunities within the British Empire. Canadian rules required travel directly from the country of origin, and only a small number of passengers were allowed ashore. Local community groups raised funds to challenge the discriminatory laws in court. The ship was eventually sent back to India, where passengers faced a confrontation with British authorities.

questions.q: Which 1950 agreement made Sikkim an Indian protectorate?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Sikkim Treaty of 1950 made Sikkim an Indian protectorate, while the other three were British-era agreements.

questions.q: What did the Korean Armistice Agreement of 1953 lead to?
options: A ceasefire without a peace treaty
Immediate reunification of the two Koreas
questions.explanation: The armistice produced a ceasefire without a peace treaty, so the two Koreas are technically still at war.

questions.q: Who led South Korea in the years after 1948?
questions.explanation: Syngman Rhee led South Korea, while Kim Il Sung led North Korea.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Sikkim was given Associate State status before it became a full state of India.
Reason (R): The 35th Constitutional Amendment created Associate State status for Sikkim in 1974.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the 1974 amendment is why Sikkim first held Associate State status.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Continuous Journey Regulation
II. Korean Armistice Agreement
III. Sikkim becomes the 22nd state of India
IV. North Korean invasion across the 38th Parallel
A. 1950
B. 1908
C. 1975
D. 1953
questions.explanation: The regulation dates to 1908, the armistice to 1953, Sikkim's statehood to 1975 and the invasion to 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Korean War ended with a formal peace treaty in 1953.
II. Sikkim became the 22nd state of India on 16 May 1975.
III. The Komagata Maru carried 376 Indian passengers to Canada in 1914.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the 1953 armistice produced no peace treaty, while II and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) Japanese occupation of Korea ended in 1945.
(b) India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission.
(c) The Indo-Sikkim Treaty of 1950 gave Sikkim Associate State status.
questions.explanation: Statements (a) and (b) are correct, while Associate State status came from the 1974 amendment, not the 1950 treaty.

quizzes.title: Korea, Komagata Maru and Sikkim: Type-in Answers
quizzes.passage:
Three episodes from the region's history are tied to recent anniversaries. The first concerns the Korean peninsula, which was split into two states after the Second World War. The dividing line has remained a border, and a demilitarised zone runs along it. Soon after the division, troops from one side crossed that line in an invasion that prompted a Security Council condemnation. The fighting ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty, so the two sides have technically remained at war.

The second episode concerns a Himalayan kingdom whose hereditary monarchs ruled for several centuries. Before its integration, a treaty made it a protectorate, and India controlled its defence, external affairs and communications. Its identity and land rights are protected by a constitutional provision. The territory later became a state of India after a popular vote.

The third episode is a voyage. A ship carried passengers from India towards Canada, where rules required travel directly from the country of origin. Only a few passengers were allowed to disembark, and the ship was eventually sent back. When passengers reached a port near Calcutta, British authorities tried to deport them, and troops opened fire. These events show how wars, migration rules and treaties shaped the status of regions and people.

questions.q: In which year was the Korean Armistice Agreement signed?
questions.explanation: The armistice was signed on 27 July 1953.

questions.q: On which day and month of 1950 did North Korean troops cross the 38th Parallel? Give the day and month.
questions.explanation: North Korean troops crossed the 38th Parallel on 25 June 1950.

questions.q: Which dynasty ruled Sikkim as hereditary monarchs from 1642 to 1975? Give the dynasty name.
questions.explanation: Sikkim was ruled by the Namgyal dynasty from 1642 to 1975.

questions.q: Who chartered the Komagata Maru?
questions.explanation: Gurdit Singh chartered the ship, also known as the Guru Nanak Jahaz.

questions.q: How many passengers were permitted to disembark at Vancouver? Give the number.
questions.explanation: Only 24 passengers were permitted to disembark on arrival in Vancouver.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave Sikkim Associate State status? Give the ordinal number.
questions.explanation: The 35th Amendment (1974) gave Sikkim Associate State status.

questions.q: Which Article protects Sikkim's cultural identity, land rights and existing laws? Give the article number with its letter.
questions.explanation: Article 371F protects Sikkim's cultural identity, land rights and existing laws.

quizzes.title: CDS, Peacekeeping and Awards: Practice MCQs
quizzes.passage:
India's Chief of Defence Staff is a four-star officer who is equivalent in rank to the three service chiefs but functions as a first among equals. The post links the armed forces with civilian political leadership, and the officer advises the defence minister on tri-service military matters. The CDS also serves as Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs in the Ministry of Defence.

The United Nations uses peacekeeping missions, which combine military, police and civilian personnel, to help countries move from conflict to peace. India is among the largest troop contributors to these missions. One such mission supervises the ceasefire between India and Pakistan in Jammu and Kashmir. Action for Peacekeeping, a UN initiative, treats women's full participation as central to peacekeeping performance. In 2025, an Indian officer serving in Lebanon received a UN award for advancing gender equality in peacekeeping.

Recognition in literature and journalism also stands out in this record. A novel translated from Mandarin Chinese recently won a major international prize for translated fiction, the first Mandarin novel to do so. Earlier Booker Prize winners include several novelists from India. The Pulitzer Prize is considered the highest national honour in the United States for journalism, literature and musical composition.

questions.q: Which committee appoints the Chief of Defence Staff?
questions.explanation: The CDS is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, which the Prime Minister chairs.

questions.q: In which year was the post of Chief of Defence Staff created?
questions.explanation: The CDS post was created in 2019 after the Kargil and Shekatkar committee recommendations.

questions.q: UN peacekeepers are often called what?
questions.explanation: UN peacekeepers are often called Blue Berets or Blue Helmets.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The CDS can hold office up to the age of 65.
Reason (R): The CDS has a fixed tenure of five years.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The age limit of 65 is correct, but the CDS has no fixed tenure, so R is false.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Kargil Review Committee
II. Shekatkar Committee
III. UN Peacekeeping founded
IV. International Day of UN Peacekeepers
A. 29 May
B. 1948
C. 2016
D. 1999
questions.explanation: The Kargil Review Committee is 1999, Shekatkar 2016, UN Peacekeeping 1948, and the Day of UN Peacekeepers 29 May.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The CDS can hold office up to the age of 70.
II. The CDS must be below 62 years of age at the time of appointment.
III. The CDS is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the maximum age for holding office is 65, while II and III are correct.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) The Pulitzer Prize is administered by Columbia University.
(b) The UN Military Gender Advocate Award was created in 2016.
(c) UN Peacekeeping was founded in 1945.
questions.explanation: Statements (a) and (b) are correct, while UN Peacekeeping was founded in 1948, so statement (c) is wrong.
